lesson.subject: maths
lesson.title: Fractions
lesson.summary: Equal parts, halves, quarters and thirds, and finding fractions of amounts.
learning_objectives: Know that fractions are equal parts of a whole
Find a half and a quarter of an amount

standards.text: Recognise, find, name and write fractions 1/3, 1/4, 2/4 and 3/4 of a length, shape, set of objects or quantity

success_criteria: I can say if parts are equal
I can name a half, a quarter and a third
I can find half of a small number
lesson.real_life: Sharing a pizza, cutting a cake and reading a clock.

warm_up.prompt: Even numbers can be split into pairs.
warm_up.explanation: Even numbers make pairs with none left over.

blocks.markdown: Today we learn about fractions: halves, quarters and thirds.
blocks.say: Welcome back, number explorer! Today we cut things into equal parts. You will meet halves, quarters and thirds. These are fractions. We use them to share fairly.

blocks.alt: A red apple cut into four slices of different sizes
blocks.caption: An apple cut into four slices.
blocks.credit: Photo by Nikolai Chernichenko on Unsplash
blocks.say: Look at this apple. It is cut into four slices. Are the slices all the same size? Have a look!

blocks.markdown:
A **fraction** is part of a **whole**. The parts must be **equal**.

Equal parts are exactly the same size.
blocks.say: A fraction is part of a whole. A whole is the complete thing, like a whole pizza. Fractions only work when the pieces are equal. Equal means exactly the same size. Look at these two cuts of pizza. In the first, the pieces are all the same size. In the second, one piece is huge and one is tiny. Only the first one is fair, so only the first one shows fractions.

blocks.alt: A pizza cut into equal parts shares fairly.
blocks.caption: A pizza cut into equal parts shares fairly.

blocks.alt: A fraction bar showing 1/2 above two quarters, showing that 1/2 = 2/4
blocks.say: Look at the two bars. One half is the same size as two quarters.

question.explanation: Equal parts are all the same size.

options.text: All the pieces are the same size

blocks.markdown:
Two equal parts make **halves**. Each part is 1/2 of the whole.

Two halves make one whole.
blocks.say: When we cut something into two equal parts, each part is a half. Two halves make one whole. We write a half like this: one over two. Look at the pizza. Two equal parts, and one is coloured. One of two equal parts is one half.

scenes.caption: A whole pizza.
scenes.say: Here is a whole pizza. We want to share it between two friends.

scenes.caption: 1 of 2 equal parts is 1/2.
scenes.say: Cut it into two equal parts. One part is coloured. One of two equal parts is one half.

blocks.title: Zara cuts the roti fairly
blocks.transcript: Zara has one whole roti. She wants to share it fairly. First she cuts it in two. Both parts are the same size. Each part is one half. Two halves make a whole. Now she cuts each half again. That makes four equal parts. Two quarters cover the same space as one half! Zara has twelve dates. She shares them into four equal groups. Three dates in each group. A quarter of twelve is three! Equal parts make fair shares. Shukriya, Zara!
blocks.caption: Zara learns halves and quarters from one roti.

points: A fraction is a part of a whole

blocks.markdown:
Four equal parts make **quarters**. Each part is 1/4 of the whole.

2 quarters make a half. 4 quarters make a whole.
blocks.say: Now cut each half in half again. That makes four equal parts. Each one is a quarter. We write a quarter as one over four. Look at the pizza. Four equal parts, and one coloured. Two quarters make a half. Four quarters make a whole. Fold a paper in half, then in half again. You can see quarters yourself!

blocks.markdown:
Three equal parts make **thirds**. Each part is 1/3.

3 thirds make a whole.
blocks.say: Cut a whole into three equal parts. Each part is a third. We write a third as one over three. A bar can show it too. Three equal parts, one coloured. One third. Three thirds make a whole.

blocks.markdown:
To find **half** of a number, share it into 2 equal groups.

Half of 8 is 4.
blocks.say: We can find a half of a group of things too. To find half, share into two equal groups. Half of eight sweets. Share eight between two. Four and four. Half of eight is four. Finding half is the same as dividing by two.

scenes.caption: 8 sweets.

scenes.caption: Half of 8 is 4.

blocks.text: Stop 2: A quarter of a number

blocks.markdown:
To find a **quarter**, share into 4 equal groups.

A quarter of 12 is 3. Or halve it twice: 12 → 6 → 3.
blocks.say: A quarter means one of four equal groups. To find a quarter, share into four equal groups. A quarter of twelve. Share twelve between four. Three in each group. A quarter of twelve is three. Here is a trick. Halve it twice. Half of twelve is six. Half of six is three.

blocks.prompt: What is a quarter of 20? Have a think first.
blocks.answer_markdown: 5. Share 20 between 4 gives 5 each. Or half of 20 is 10, and half of 10 is 5.

question.explanation: Half of 8 is 4. Half of 4 is 2.

points: Half means share into 2 equal groups
A quarter means share into 4 equal groups
Halve twice to find a quarter
blocks.say: Remember. Half means share into two. A quarter means share into four. Halving twice gives a quarter.

terms.meaning: To cut or share into two equal parts.

blocks.markdown:
Fractions help us share. 4 quarters share between 2 people gives 2 quarters each, which is 1/2.

More people means each share is smaller.
blocks.say: Fractions help us share fairly. Ayesha and her brother share a pizza cut in four equal parts. They each eat two parts. Two quarters is one half. So each of them eats half the pizza. If four friends share it, each gets one quarter. The more people, the smaller each share.

scenes.say: A pizza is cut into four equal parts. Ayesha and her brother share it.

scenes.caption: Each person gets 2 quarters = 1/2.
scenes.say: Each person has two quarters. Two quarters is one half. Each person gets half the pizza.

blocks.markdown: Look around and spot halves, quarters and thirds in everyday things.
blocks.say: Look around your home and find fractions. A clock face shows quarters. A chocolate bar has equal pieces. A sandwich cut in half. A packet of biscuits shared between four. What fractions can you spot today? Draw them in your book.
